concerns.concern: LED heating has not been ruled out as the cause of the light-induced erasure. The LED sits 1 cm from the sample, heating jumps are visible, and warming is already known to reset the gate-cycling enhancement. An independent measurement of sample temperature during illumination is needed.
concerns.quote: A transient local temperature rise during illumination could therefore produce some or all of the "erasure."

concerns.concern: A dark-warming control is needed. The gate-cycled sample should be warmed without light to several temperatures (e.g. 20, 40, 100, 150 K), re-cooled, and its T_c and R_s compared with the illuminated case.
concerns.quote: A control in which the gate-cycled sample is warmed in the dark to various temperatures (e.g., 20, 40, 100, 150 K) and re-cooled

concerns.concern: The T_c changes may simply follow the established KTO(111) relationship between T_c and mobility/confinement, which would make PNR-mediated pairing unnecessary. The authors should plot T_c against μ and against n for all states and see whether the points collapse onto one curve.
concerns.quote: The observations may therefore reflect the established T_c–μ (confinement) relationship, with the memory living in the electrostatic profile set by trapped charge.

concerns.concern: The authors call the drop in T_c under illumination, despite higher n and μ, counterintuitive. The reviewer argues it is actually expected from prior work showing that T_c tracks mobility or confinement rather than carrier density.
concerns.quote: The authors state that the reduction of T_c by illumination, despite higher n and μ, is "counterintuitive."

concerns.concern: The dielectric data have not been shown to carry the gate and light history. The authors should check whether the loss peaks change in amplitude or position after gate cycling and after illumination.
concerns.quote: Do the loss peaks change in amplitude or position after gate cycling, and again after illumination?

concerns.concern: The dielectric measurement spans the full 0.5 mm of bulk KTO. The loss peaks may therefore be bulk properties with no relevance to the interface where the 2DEG lives.
concerns.quote: Its sensitivity to the interfacial region where the 2DEG lives is negligible. Peaks 1 and 2 may be bulk properties

concerns.concern: Thermally activated loss peaks with activation energies of a few hundred meV are typical of Maxwell–Wagner interfacial polarization, for example from contacts or depletion layers. This artefact must be excluded, e.g. by varying electrode material or substrate thickness, or by checking Debye/Kramers–Kronig consistency.
concerns.quote: Thermally activated loss peaks with activation energies of a few hundred meV are a classic signature of interfacial (Maxwell–Wagner) polarization.

concerns.concern: The integrated anomalous gate current (~10^13–10^14 e/cm²) appears one to two orders of magnitude larger than the change in 2DEG density. The authors should integrate I_g explicitly and account for where the charge goes.
concerns.quote: That is one to two orders of magnitude larger than the change in 2DEG density (~2–4 × 10¹² cm⁻²

concerns.concern: The text describes two minima in the relaxation time τ at 35 K and 95 K. In Fig. 4c, however, τ at 95 K is the largest value in the data set, and the minimum in that region lies near 85–90 K.
concerns.quote: τ has a minimum near 30–35 K, but at 95 K it is the largest value in the data set (~1.38 × 10³ s).

concerns.concern: The relaxation curves at 35 K and 95 K look anomalous and noisy. R_s appears to overshoot the pre-illumination value, and the ΔR/R₁ maxima each rest on a single point. A similar protocol in Supp. Fig. 5a shows no such anomalies, so these measurements should be repeated with finer temperature steps and temperature stability confirmed.
concerns.quote: R_s at these temperatures appears to rise in the dark by considerably more than the illumination-induced drop, overshooting the pre-illumination value.

concerns.concern: "Erasure of superconductivity" in the title and abstract is misleading. Only a ~50–70 mK (5–7%) gate-induced T_c enhancement is undone, on a transition ~0.3 K wide.
concerns.quote: Superconductivity is never erased. What is erased is a gate-induced T_c enhancement of roughly 50–70 mK (about 5–7%)

concerns.concern: Complete erasure is not demonstrated. The final illuminated state L₄ is never compared with the pristine, as-cooled transition.
concerns.quote: It never compares L₄ with the pristine, as-cooled transition (the dashed curve in Fig. 1d).

concerns.concern: The post-illumination R_s baseline and the pristine R_s were measured at different temperatures (10 K vs 1.4 K), so they cannot be compared to support a reset to baseline.
concerns.quote: The R_s baseline after illumination (795 Ω at 10 K) cannot be compared with the pristine R_s (~745 Ω at 1.4 K)

concerns.concern: The Discussion itself says the system does not fully recover, which contradicts the claim of complete erasure.
concerns.quote: It states that "the system does not fully recover to the pre-illumination state."

concerns.concern: The argument that red light activates the processes because the photon energy exceeds their activation energies is physically unsound. PNR reorientation is not an optically allowed transition, so a coupling mechanism is needed.
concerns.quote: Photon energy exceeding a thermal activation barrier does not imply that the photon couples to that process.

concerns.concern: Illumination at 2 K produces no change in R_s, unlike at 10 and 15 K. This contradicts the claim that the process is photo-activated even at extremely low temperatures.
concerns.quote: If the process were photo-activated independently of temperature, the 2 K result should not be null.

concerns.concern: Because erasure does not work at 2 K, device operation would require thermal cycling between about 10 K and below 1 K. This limitation should be acknowledged in the neuromorphic discussion.
concerns.quote: erasure cannot be done at the temperature where superconductivity is used.

concerns.concern: The PNR assignment is made by analogy with Li-doped KTO, and PNRs in pure KTO are debated. Direct probes are needed: thermally stimulated depolarization or current after poling, Raman/SHG, or P–E loops.
concerns.quote: Without such data, "PNR flipping" remains an assignment by analogy with Li-doped KTO literature

concerns.concern: The linear relation between Δ_L and ε is weak evidence, because both rise monotonically on cooling and will give a near-linear plot over a limited range almost regardless of the physics.
concerns.quote: Both Δ_L and ε rise monotonically on cooling, so plotting one against the other will produce a smooth, nearly linear curve

concerns.concern: The slope change near 35 K in the Δ_L–ε correlation rests on only a handful of points.
concerns.quote: A change in slope near 35 K, defined by a handful of points, is weak evidence.

concerns.concern: The claimed onset of Δ_L at 95 K corresponds to Δ_L ≈ 0, apparently within the noise level.
concerns.quote: The "onset" at 95 K corresponds to Δ_L ≈ 0 within what appears to be the noise level.

concerns.concern: ε was measured in the small-signal limit, but Δ_L involves ±50 V sweeps where KTO's field-tunable permittivity matters. The Δ_L ∝ (ε − ε_∞) argument is only qualitative; error bars and a quantitative model are needed.
concerns.quote: ε was measured in the small-signal limit, whereas Δ_L involves ±50 V sweeps, where the field tunability of KTO's ε is relevant.

concerns.concern: It is unclear where the deep donor traps are located, and whether a negative back-gate field is consistent with electrons tunnelling back into them.
concerns.quote: A negative back-gate pushes electrons toward the AlOₓ side. The authors should specify where these deep donors are

concerns.concern: The remnant PNR polarization needed to explain the hysteretic Δn should be estimated, and its plausibility for PNRs in KTO assessed.
concerns.quote: please estimate the required remnant polarization from the hysteretic Δn and assess whether it is plausible for PNRs in KTO.

concerns.concern: The irreversible gate asymmetry appears on the negative branch, whereas in LAO/STO it is typically tied to the first positive sweep. The authors should discuss that literature and explain the sign.
concerns.quote: The authors should discuss this literature and explain why the asymmetry here appears on the negative branch.

concerns.concern: The text's distinction between "voltage variance" and "displacement current" is incorrect, since all of I_g is displacement current in the linear regime. It should be rephrased as reversible capacitive versus irreversible trapping/leakage contributions.
concerns.quote: all of I_g is displacement current in the linear regime.

concerns.concern: The relaxation fits are poorly constrained because τ (~10³ s) is comparable to the observation window. Fit uncertainties should be given, and a stretched exponential may suit glassy defect dynamics better.
concerns.quote: τ (~10³ s) is comparable to the observation window (~2 × 10³ s). For glassy defect dynamics, a stretched exponential may be more appropriate.

concerns.concern: The novelty relative to Ref. 30 is unclear, since gate-cycling T_c enhancement and its thermal reset were already reported there. The authors should state what is new and compare magnitudes and mechanisms.
concerns.quote: Please state clearly what is new here (presumably the optical reset and the dielectric correlation) and compare the magnitudes and mechanisms.

concerns.concern: T_c is defined at 50% of R_N while R_N itself changes. Onset and zero-resistance T_c, and ideally H_c2 or I_c, should be shown to rule out artefacts from transition width or inhomogeneity.
concerns.quote: T_c uses a 50%-of-R_N criterion while R_N itself changes. Please also show onset and zero-resistance T_c, and ideally H_c2 or I_c

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether all data come from a single sample. Results on multiple samples, ideally with different oxygen-vacancy densities, are needed to test the OV assignment.
concerns.quote: Please report results on multiple samples, ideally with different OV densities (reduction conditions) to test the OV assignment.

concerns.concern: The non-volatile and neuromorphic claims need retention data over hours to days and endurance over many more than about 8 cycles.
concerns.quote: retention data (R_s and T_c versus time over hours to days at fixed temperature) and endurance over many more than ~8 cycles are needed.

concerns.concern: n and μ were extracted from three separate runs assumed to be identical. Because the effects are only a few percent, run-to-run reproducibility and error bars must be shown.
concerns.quote: The effects are small (Δn/n ~ 1–2%, Δμ/μ ~ 4%), so run-to-run reproducibility must be demonstrated and error bars shown.

concerns.concern: Multiband effects in the Hall analysis are not discussed.
concerns.quote: Please comment on multiband effects in the Hall analysis.

concerns.concern: ε′ reportedly shows no frequency dispersion while tan δ has frequency-dependent peaks. ε′ and ε″ should be shown separately and without vertical offsets.
concerns.quote: Please show ε′ and ε″ separately and without vertical offsets.

concerns.concern: The 5 V AC excitation is large for a gate-history-dependent material, so the amplitude dependence of the dielectric response should be shown.
concerns.quote: A 5 V AC excitation is large for a material whose state the authors show to be gate-history dependent. Please show amplitude dependence

concerns.concern: The device state (pristine, cycled, or illuminated) in which the dielectric data were taken is not specified.
concerns.quote: state which state (pristine, cycled, illuminated) the dielectric data were taken in.

concerns.concern: The optical power or power density at the sample and the LED drive conditions are not given. The Methods ambiguously say both current and voltage were kept the same.
concerns.quote: The Methods say both I_L and V_L were "kept the same"; please clarify which.

concerns.concern: The LED emission spectrum at cryogenic temperature should be provided, since it blue-shifts on cooling.
concerns.quote: The LED emission spectrum at cryogenic temperature, which blue-shifts on cooling.

concerns.concern: The dependence on wavelength, including at least one longer-wavelength source below the defect levels, and on optical power at fixed dose should be measured.
concerns.quote: The dependence on wavelength, at least one longer-wavelength source (e.g., IR, below the relevant defect levels), and the dependence on optical power at fixed dose.

concerns.concern: The dependence of R_s on cycling sequence (Type A vs Type B) follows directly from the hysteresis loop. It should be presented as a restatement rather than an additional finding.
concerns.quote: This is a restatement of the hysteresis rather than an additional finding, and should be presented as such.

concerns.concern: ε appears to peak near 10 K and decrease below, whereas pure KTO usually saturates. This may indicate an extrinsic contribution.
concerns.quote: ε appears to peak near ~10 K and decrease below. Pure KTO usually saturates. Please comment; this could indicate an extrinsic contribution.

concerns.concern: tan δ obtained as π/2 − θ is very sensitive to instrumental phase offsets, especially at 4 kHz, and the phase calibration is not described.
concerns.quote: tan δ ≈ π/2 − θ is very sensitive to instrumental phase offsets, especially at 4 kHz. Please describe the phase calibration.

concerns.concern: The OV charge-state transition corresponding to 236 meV is not identified, and calling the OVs "shallow" conflicts with that activation energy. An explicit energy-level diagram with numbers is requested.
concerns.quote: Please specify which transition corresponds to 236 meV. Also reconcile the "shallow OV" language with an activation energy of 236 meV

concerns.concern: Fig. 2b lacks the illumination duration and power, and does not explain why the 15 K trace relaxes while the 10 K trace does not.
concerns.quote: Please give the illumination duration and power. Why does the 15 K trace show relaxation while the 10 K trace does not?

concerns.concern: The AlOₓ thickness is missing from the Methods.
concerns.quote: Please state the AlOₓ thickness, which is missing from the Methods.

concerns.concern: The Methods' justification that van der Pauw transport measurements minimise fringe effects in dielectric measurements is unclear.
concerns.quote: "In order to minimise fringe effect in dielectric measurements, the transport measurements were conducted in van der Pauw method" needs clarification.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3e caption describes the polarization direction ambiguously. It should be defined relative to the 2DEG and the gate.
concerns.quote: "Pointing outwards to the interface" versus "inwards away from the interface" is ambiguous.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3 caption says "deviates above" instead of explicitly stating a steeper slope below 35 K. It also places a T = 35 K line in panel d, whose x-axis is ε rather than T.
concerns.quote: the "T = 35 K" dashed line is said to appear in panel d, which has ε, not T, on the x-axis.

concerns.concern: Notation in Supp. Note 4 is inconsistent with the main text, and the elevated 856 Ω value is mislabelled with the baseline symbol.
concerns.quote: Item 2 labels the elevated value 856 Ω as "R_s^b" (the baseline symbol), which appears to be a typo.

concerns.concern: The claim of a "previously unrecognized interplay" is an overstatement given existing Refs. 30, 43 and 44.
concerns.quote: "previously unrecognized interplay" is an overstatement given Refs. 30, 43, 44

concerns.concern: The Discussion repeats the same idea in two consecutive sentences.
concerns.quote: The Discussion repeats the same idea in two consecutive sentences

concerns.concern: Supplementary Fig. 5 is mislabelled as "Extended Figure 5."
concerns.quote: Supp. Fig. 5 is captioned "Extended Figure 5."

concerns.concern: There are several wording errors and typos, e.g. "laser emitting diode," "tangent loss," "memrisitive," and "illlumination."
concerns.quote: "laser emitting diode" → light-emitting diode
